notes: RBox: functionality removed. In common-practice tonal theory each major and minor key has exactly one key signature (D major two sharps, E-flat major three flats); enharmonic spellings such as C-sharp and D-flat major are different keys with their own signatures, so they are not exceptions. Relations with real exceptions were rejected: 'was written by' (co-authored works), 'is housed in' (works co-owned by two museums), 'was originally written in' (macaronic works). Baroque 'Dorian' notation of minor-key pieces with one flat fewer is a practice of notating a piece, not a second signature of the key; instances use major keys to stay clear of it (R1). The instances ask whether one value excludes another. New answers: direct no, both instances no, cross-lingual no, balancing 0017 (all yes). Near query: 'is the dominant of' functional? (yes: G is the dominant of C only), which the edit leaves alone and whose answer differs from the new one (R7). has_key_signature is a new relation, in the scratch file relations/literature_arts.rbox2.md.
